answer: Each seat must keep its own hive on a surveyed stand behind the reef coast, tagged with a numbered copper seal. At enrollment a lab isolates the nectar yeast from that hive and records its genomic fingerprint; a second seat claiming the same fingerprint is refused and the tag's bond is forfeited. One stand holds one hive, a colony takes a full season before its yeast is distinguishable, and every stand is walked in person. Cloning cannot outrun biology: seats appear no faster than hives already a season old, and each extra identity costs its own site, its own season, and a forfeitable bond.
